Version-2 contract: docs/storage-text-format.md. UTF-8/LF sorted JSON per immutable UUID project record, preserved integer API aliases with original SQL allocation semantics in every domain and sequential task/QA display numbers, UUID foreign-key references, exact multiline chunks, explicit ordering and deletion tombstones. Preserve authoritative schema-14 project domains and QA evidence. Application request history is excluded from Git: retry results, machine paths, intents and execution ownership remain in ignored checkout-local state shared by desktop/MCP. Reads, fresh no-op requests and retries leave tracked bytes and mtimes unchanged; fresh clones have no request history or cross-clone replay guarantee. Version-1 projects remain read-only byte-stable; the next successful content write upgrades the format and removes legacy request files with recoverable journal deletion, retaining local retry results. Conversions emit version 2 and preserve local retry results within the same checkout. Reuse domain validators through a disposable in-memory SQLite projection. SHA-256 resource fingerprints reject stale content despite equal branch counters. Shared local OS lock, before/after journal and atomic replacement protect cooperating clients and interrupted writes; unexpected external edits block recovery. No Git commands or automatic conflict resolution. Full structural/semantic validation rejects markers, invalid references, collisions, duplicate task/QA link positions and unsafe artifacts. O(project size) materialization; external Git writes must remain idle during publication; directory durability is platform dependent. Task 19 verifies real independent-clone Git scenarios and native WebView2/MCP pull, branch, conflict, no-op and migration flows. Native conflict reload preserves drafts without autosaving discarded edits. Evidence and practical limits: docs/storage-git-collaboration.md.

Approved Markdown extension (implementation pending): Extend the current version-2 canonical JSON record vocabulary and any explicitly versioned upgrade needed for Markdown records and typed associations. Store complete prose in canonical records using the existing exact multiline representation; generated .md exports never become authoritative text-backend records. Update closed collection/schema inventories, UUID/reference mapping, aliases, tombstones, ordering, semantic validation, resource fingerprints, local receipts, journal recovery, export/import and disposable relational materialization. Preserve stable identities across Git clones and backend conversion; reject merge markers/invalid references and same-resource stale writes rather than auto-merging. Compatibility reads do not rewrite old projects, unchanged files stay byte/mtime-stable, and upgrades occur only via supported explicit/write migration paths. Verify independent edits merge normally and overlapping edits remain visible conflicts. Keep request history and machine-specific output state out of tracked canonical records.

Task numbering correction (2026-09-25): Tasks use short increasing numeric API IDs and display numbers on every backend. In text storage, reserve task IDs above the maximum live or tombstoned task ID without a random gap; allocate task display numbers as the current project maximum plus one, matching SQLite. UUID record identities and UUID foreign-key references remain canonical. Independent offline clones can allocate the same task ID/number; detect and reject such merges, then explicitly reconcile numeric aliases and task resource-version keys while preserving UUID references. Never silently renumber during reads. The user-authorized correction of the twelve Markdown planning tasks maps API IDs to 25-36 and display numbers to 22-33, preserving their UUID identities, design links and updating saved textual dependency references. Historical local operation receipts remain original responses, not current task snapshots.

All-domain numeric ID compatibility (2026-09-25; supersedes the task-only allocator correction): Numeric IDs and human task/QA numbers must retain the pre-adapter SQL behavior in every adapter. Reference baseline is commit f96fca1. All AUTOINCREMENT-backed domains allocate after their highest live, deleted or consumed sequence ID without random gaps; task and QA numbers use the existing project MAX(number)+1 rule. The text adapter restores and retains those sequence high-water marks as existing-format minimal tombstones, including IDs consumed by upserts with no added row, on successful writes and both conversion directions. Centralized sequences.rs is shared by writes and migration; failed transactions, retries and no-ops retain existing semantics. UUID filenames/foreign-key record identities remain internal storage identities; caller-supplied design/note identifiers and opaque concurrency tokens keep their existing contracts. Existing persisted business IDs must not be bulk-renumbered implicitly. Independent clones can collide in any numeric collection; reads report collisions without silently remapping. Conformance compares actual domain allocations, continued writes after upserts and conversion, and every numeric table high-water mark. Future server SQL must implement the same contract instead of introducing a new allocation policy.
